title: Bellerophon Sent Against the Chimera

scope.description: Bellerophon's false accusation leads to a deadly commission against the Chimera and divine aid from Minerva.
scope.boundaryRationale: The selected passages stop at Minerva's bridle; the later Chimera fight is not inferred.

sourceBoundaryDecision: The selected passages stop at Minerva's bridle; the later Chimera fight is not inferred.

evidence.sourceText: Bellerophon, a brave young prince, the grandson of Sisyphus, King of Corinth, had the great misfortune to kill his own brother while hunting in the forest.

He had not sojourned there very long, before Anteia, the queen, fell in love with him; and although her husband, Prœtus, treated her with the utmost kindness, she made up her mind to desert him, and tried to induce Bellerophon to elope with her.

He had not sojourned there very long, before Anteia, the queen, fell in love with him; and although her husband, Prœtus, treated her with the utmost kindness, she made up her mind to desert him, and tried to induce Bellerophon to elope with her.

Prœtus, indignant at what he deemed deep treachery on the part of an honored guest, yet reluctant to punish him with his own hand as he deserved, sent Bellerophon to Iobates, King of Lycia, with a sealed message bidding him put the bearer to death.

While thus inwardly bewailing the ill luck which had so persistently dogged his footsteps, Bellerophon suddenly saw Minerva appear before him in all her splendor, and heard her inquire in gentle tones the cause of his too evident dejection.

He had no sooner apprised her of the difficult task appointed him, than she promised him her aid, and before she vanished gave him a beautiful golden bridle, which she bade him use to control Pegasus.

He had no sooner apprised her of the difficult task appointed him, than she promised him her aid, and before she vanished gave him a beautiful golden bridle, which she bade him use to control Pegasus.

He did not like to take a stranger's life, and still could not refuse to comply with Prœtus' urgent request: so, after much thought, he decided to send Bellerophon to attack the Chimæra, a terrible monster with a lion's head, a goat's body, and a dragon's tail.

narrative.synopsis: After Anteia falsely accuses Bellerophon, Proetus sends him to Iobates with a deadly letter. Iobates assigns him the Chimera, and Minerva gives him a bridle for Pegasus.
narrative.openingSituation: Bellerophon is received by Proetus after fleeing Corinth.
narrative.centralConflict: False accusation turns royal hospitality into a death commission.
narrative.resolution: Minerva supplies the bridle needed to control Pegasus.
narrative.outcome: Bellerophon is prepared for the Chimera task, but the fight itself lies outside this source boundary.

Minerva gave Bellerophon a golden bridle to control Pegasus.
